priorities.label: Water conservation
priorities.description: Preferring rotations whose crops use less water over the season.
priorities.evidence_requirement: Seasonal crop water use for every crop in the rotation, calculated for the local climate, together with the season's rainfall. A published water-need range alone is not enough.
limitations: Indicative seasonal water needs exist for maize, sorghum and common bean only. Cowpea and mung bean have crop coefficients but no seasonal figure; pigeon pea has neither.
All values describe well-watered crops, so they show potential water use, not what a rain-fed crop would actually use.

priorities.label: Nitrogen-fixing potential
priorities.description: Preferring rotations that include crops able to fix nitrogen from the air.
priorities.evidence_requirement: Which crops fix nitrogen, and how much of it remains in the field after harvest for the following crop under local conditions.
limitations: The knowledge base records which crops are described as nitrogen-fixing. It does not hold how much nitrogen any of them leaves for the next crop.
The review read reports that the size of the benefit varies widely between sites and is not well explained.

priorities.label: Erosion reduction
priorities.description: Preferring rotations that keep the soil covered and protected.
priorities.evidence_requirement: How long each rotation leaves the soil bare, the slope of the field, and how intense the rain is when the soil is bare.
limitations: Only a general principle about soil cover is held. There are no local planting calendars, no slope data and no sub-daily rainfall intensity.
The NASA rainfall used is a daily average over a large grid cell, which smooths the intense storms that cause erosion.

priorities.label: Organic matter improvement
priorities.description: Preferring rotations that build soil organic matter.
priorities.evidence_requirement: Measured change in soil organic matter under each rotation, or the amount of residue each rotation returns to the soil.
limitations: The evidence held points the other way from what is often assumed: the review read says studies generally report no impact of grain legumes on soil organic matter.
No residue quantities are held for any crop.

priorities.label: Forage value
priorities.description: Preferring rotations that also produce feed for livestock.
priorities.evidence_requirement: Forage yield and feed quality of each crop under local conditions, and whether the farmer keeps livestock.
limitations: No forage yields or feed values were extracted, although several of the datasheets read are about forage use.
This priority must be shown as needing local information, not scored.

priorities.label: Market and economic considerations
priorities.description: Preferring rotations whose crops can be sold or are worth growing economically.
priorities.evidence_requirement: Current local prices, costs and demand for each crop. These change from season to season and place to place.
limitations: No prices, costs or returns are held, and none are estimated.
The Machakos experiment reported higher profitability for legume-based systems between 1989 and 1996. That historical result is not used as a present-day economic estimate.
This priority must be shown as needing local information, not scored.

priorities.label: Pest and disease cycle disruption
priorities.description: Preferring rotations that interrupt the build-up of pests and diseases.
priorities.evidence_requirement: Which pests and diseases affect each crop locally, which crops host them, and how long they survive without a host.
limitations: Only a general principle is held. The review read says evidence on pest and disease effects of legume rotations in sub-Saharan Africa is lacking.
No pest or disease is recorded for any specific crop pair, and nothing is held about crops of the same family.

priorities.label: Resilience across dry and wet seasons
priorities.description: Preferring rotations that hold up across the range of seasons the area has experienced.
priorities.evidence_requirement: A comparison of each rotation under dry, typical and wet historical seasons, using crop water use, drought sensitivity and the validated NASA record. This is the work of phase A4.
limitations: The inputs exist for some crops only, and no comparison has been made yet.
A record of past seasons cannot show how a rotation will perform in a climate that is changing.

priorities.label: Crop diversity
priorities.description: Preferring rotations with more different crops and plant families.
priorities.evidence_requirement: The crops in the rotation and the botanical family of each.
limitations: Counting crops and families is descriptive. It does not by itself show any benefit.
The knowledge base holds only two families, so the measure can distinguish little.

priorities.label: Operational simplicity
priorities.description: Preferring rotations that are simpler to manage with the labour and equipment available.
priorities.evidence_requirement: Labour, equipment and timing demands of each crop on the farm in question.
limitations: No labour or equipment information is held.
This priority must be shown as needing local information, not scored.
